chapter_theme: A single song at Somanathan Madam (சோமநாதன்மடம்): the poet asks for the sword of teaching in the silent word, which strikes down Yama's servants, so that body, life and wandering heart melt; the praise honours Somanathan, the ascetic who worships the Lord of Arunai and founded the monastery, and Murugan who never grows angry with his devotees' many wants.

824.reading: The poet speaks of the passion, infatuation and enjoyment that wander daily and never go one way, with maya and the two deeds never leaving him, and asks that, so his body, life and a heart that never stays a moment in awareness of the Lord may melt, Murugan give him the sword of teaching in the silent word, called the steadfast yoga of Siva-knowledge where night and day are gone, which strikes Yama's servants who fling the noose in anger, and so end his enemies. The praise names the monastery of Somanathan, praised on earth, a wise man who never fails in the worship of the Lord of Arunai who is half woman, death to the Jains' clan, a king among ascetics; Murugan who broke the Sura army and Meru; and the god who never knows anger though countless devotees state their wants.
824.nuance: மோன உரையில் உபதேச வாள்: the teaching given in silence is a sword against Death's servants, joining the two common pleas (the guru's word, rescue at death). The praise honours a human founder, சோமநாதன், as அமணர் குல காலன், the same title the poet gives Sambandar. The last line, முனிய அறியாத தேவர், praises the Lord's patience with petitioners.

links.note: Tirumular says that for those whom silence reaches, release and the powers come and all speech ends in a mute word; 824 makes that silent word the guru's teaching, a sword that drives off Death's servants.

824 asks for the sword of teaching in the silent word (மோன உரையில் உபதேச வாளை) so that body, life and the wandering heart melt. Tirumanthiram 2648 says the guru told him the one thing beyond telling (உரையற்ற தொன்றை உரைத்தான்), cut off craving for the arts and entered him. Both describe a teaching that is spoken yet wordless and that cuts; the Tirumanthiram reports its effect, the song asks for it as a weapon against Yama's servants.
